description.narrative: The recent earthquakes in Myanmar have deepened an already fragile humanitarian crisis, particularly in Mandalay, Sagaing, and Magway regions. Thousands of households are now in critical need. Rapid assessments identified cash assistance, and shelter are the most urgent requirement—71% of surveyed families reported their cash reserves would be depleted within a week, threatening their access to food, water, shelter, and medicine. Pre-existing economic instability has been further exacerbated by the disaster. Based on the needs assessment reports and the HNRP Flash Addendum on the Myanmar Earthquake (April 2025), a total of 1.1 million people are identified as newly in need of assistance. Of these: 739,000 people require Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), 753,000 people are in need of Shelter and Non-Food Items (NFIs), and 1 million people require Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) support. In response, a targeted, conflict-sensitive humanitarian intervention is being launched in collaboration with lead and implementing partners Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW), Muslim Aid (MA), NCRA, NHM, and PSSAG to reach and cover the most affected areas and critical needs. This includes Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) for 3,800 families as per cluster standard, along with essential Non-Food Items—tarpaulins/plastic sheets for 380 families, plastic buckets for 380 families, emergency bamboo shelter 80 units and toilet 60 units for around 800 people. Total 20,408 earthquake affected individuals regardless of age, gender and diversity will be benefitted from this action. The intervention prioritizes dignity, choice, and resilience, empowering affected families to meet their most pressing needs. MPCA offers flexibility, stimulates local markets, and supports both immediate relief and longer-term recovery, in line with the DEC Theory of Change.Grounded in conflict sensitivity, the program integrates localized risk analysis, community-based targeting, and robust feedback mechanisms to ensure equitable and safe delivery. A strong protection lens prioritizes marginalized and at-risk groups, including persons with disabilities, elderly individuals, female-headed households, and those with chronic illnesses. Customized outreach strategies enhance accessibility and safety for all.In its initial phase, the program will deliver MPCA, NFIs, emergency shelters, and toilets to meet survival and protection needs, reducing reliance on negative coping strategies. Total 20,208 people will be directly benefitted from this initiatives.As part of a broader triple nexus approach, the initiative will transition from emergency response to sustainable recovery. Future phases will focus on constructing permanent shelters and WASH facilities, restoring livelihoods, supporting micro-enterprises, and strengthening value chains—building long-term community resilience and stability.
